newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma names new chief crime buster.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma names new chief crime buster.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma, under pressure from western governments to clean up corruption, on Thursday named one of Ukraine's most experienced politicians to head a new National Bureau of Investigation.
Vasyl Durdynets, who has held a string of senior posts under Kuchma and his predecessor Leonid Kravchuk, will give up his post as first deputy prime minister, a presidential spokesman said.

He said Durdynets' appointment to the body set up to fight corruption and organised crime in the former Soviet republic was part of the cabinet reshuffle launched last week after the appointment of new Prime Minister Valery Pustovoitenko.
The spokesman said Kuchma also re-appointed Yuri Kostenko as Environment Minister.
Kostenko heads Ukraine's delegation at talks with Group of Seven wealthy countries on the closure of the Chernobyl nuclear plant, whose fourth reactor blew up in 1986, by 2000.

The spokesman also said Kuchma moved Anatoly Minchenko from his post as state minister in charge of energy issues to become head of the Committee on Material Resources which oversees Ukraine's natural resources.
Kuchma, who left Kiev on Wednesday evening for a three-week holiday in the Crimean peninsula, must still fill several posts.

They include ministers of transport, justice, information and youth and family matters as well as heads of the Security Service (SBU) and National Bureau for Reconstruction and Development, which deals with foreign investments.
